engines.name: Unity
engines.how: Mono builds keep the game's code in Data/Managed/*.dll, which runs with the Unity player of the same version for another platform (found in a Unity install, or downloaded once from Unity: only the player, no Unity install needed). The build's shaders must cover the target's graphics API, and native plugins need their own builds. IL2CPP builds are native code and need the source.

engines.name: Unreal Engine
engines.how: The game code is compiled into the executable. A native port needs the project source; otherwise run the Windows build through a compatibility layer.

engines.name: Godot
engines.how: Scripts and assets live in the .pck (or inside the .exe). The same .pck runs with the Godot export template of the same version for the target.

engines.name: RAGE (Rockstar Advanced Game Engine)
engines.how: Native engine code. Without source, only a compatibility layer (or a hosted/streamed build) can run it elsewhere.

engines.name: Source
engines.how: Native engine code. Without source, only a compatibility layer can run it elsewhere.

engines.name: GameMaker
engines.how: data.win holds the game; it needs a GameMaker runner for the target. Compatibility varies by version.

engines.name: Ren'Py
engines.how: The game/ folder (.rpa, .rpyc) runs on any platform with the Ren'Py runtime of the same version.

engines.name: RPG Maker MV/MZ
engines.how: MV/MZ games are HTML5 + JavaScript: the web folder runs in a browser, in a WebKit app on macOS, or with NW.js on Windows and Linux.

engines.name: RPG Maker XP/VX/VX Ace
engines.how: The game's Ruby scripts and data run on mkxp-z, an open-source RGSS runtime for macOS and Linux. Windows keeps the original Game.exe. Games that use the RTP need it installed.

engines.name: LÖVE
engines.how: The game is a .love archive of Lua scripts and assets (on its own or fused into the .exe). It runs with the official LÖVE build of the same version for each platform.

engines.name: HTML5 (Construct, GDevelop, Twine, NW.js, Electron)
engines.how: The game is a web page: it runs in a browser, in a WebKit app on macOS, or with NW.js on Windows and Linux. Electron games that call Node.js need those parts changed.

engines.name: macOS app / Mach-O
engines.how: Already a macOS build. Porting Toolkit can still apply advanced options and community patches.

engines.name: Construct
engines.how: Web games: the HTML5 plugins export them (browser, WebKit app on macOS, NW.js on Windows and Linux).

engines.name: GDevelop
engines.how: Web games: the HTML5 plugins export them (browser, WebKit app on macOS, NW.js on Windows and Linux).

engines.name: Phaser
engines.how: Web games: the HTML5 plugins export them (browser, WebKit app on macOS, NW.js on Windows and Linux).

engines.how: Web games: the HTML5 plugins export them (browser, WebKit app on macOS, NW.js on Windows and Linux).

engines.how: Web games: the HTML5 plugins export them (browser, WebKit app on macOS, NW.js on Windows and Linux).

engines.how: Web games: the HTML5 plugins export them (browser, WebKit app on macOS, NW.js on Windows and Linux).

engines.name: Turbulenz
engines.how: Web games: the HTML5 plugins export them (browser, WebKit app on macOS, NW.js on Windows and Linux).

engines.name: SCUMM (LucasArts)
engines.how: The game's data files run on ScummVM, which reimplements SCUMM for every platform.

engines.name: Adventure Game Interpreter (Sierra AGI)
engines.how: The game's resource files (LOGDIR, PICDIR, VOL.*) run on ScummVM.

engines.name: Adventure Game Studio
engines.how: AGS games keep their data in ac2game.dat, a .ags file or appended to the .exe; ScummVM runs them on every platform.

engines.name: Wintermute Engine
engines.how: Wintermute games keep their data in .dcp packages, which ScummVM runs on every platform.

engines.name: Freescape (Incentive Software)
engines.how: ScummVM runs the DOS releases of Driller, Dark Side, Total Eclipse and Castle Master.

engines.name: Doom engine (id Tech 1)
engines.how: The game's IWAD (DOOM.WAD, DOOM2.WAD, HERETIC.WAD...) runs on a Doom source port for every platform.

engines.name: Quake engine
engines.how: Quake's id1/ folder (pak0.pak, pak1.pak) runs on QuakeSpasm or vkQuake.

engines.name: id Tech 2 (Quake II)
engines.how: Quake II's baseq2/ folder runs on Yamagi Quake II.

engines.name: Jake2
engines.how: Jake2 is a Java port of Quake II. Quake II's own data (baseq2/) runs on Yamagi Quake II with the quake2-export plugin.

engines.name: id Tech 3 (Quake III Arena)
engines.how: Quake III Arena's baseq3/ folder runs on ioquake3. Other id Tech 3 games need their own source ports.

engines.name: ioquake3
engines.how: ioquake3 is itself the open source port of id Tech 3. Quake III Arena's baseq3/ data runs on it with the quake3-export plugin.

engines.name: id Tech 4 (Doom 3)
engines.how: Doom 3 and Resurrection of Evil (base/*.pk4) run on dhewm3. Quake 4 and Prey are not supported by it.

engines.name: Wolfenstein 3D engine
engines.how: The game's data files (VSWAP.WL6, GAMEMAPS.WL6...) run on ECWolf.

engines.name: Build engine
engines.how: Duke Nukem 3D, Blood, Shadow Warrior and other Build games run on Raze with their original data.

engines.name: Jedi engine (Dark Forces)
engines.how: Dark Forces' .GOB files run on The Force Engine.

engines.name: GoldSrc (Half-Life engine)
engines.how: Half-Life's valve/ folder runs on Xash3D FWGS (the game's own DLLs need builds for the target; Valve's are Windows only).

engines.name: Infinity Engine
engines.how: Baldur's Gate, Icewind Dale and Planescape: Torment data (chitin.key, .bif) run on GemRB.

engines.name: OpenMW (Morrowind)
engines.how: Morrowind's Data Files (Morrowind.esm, .bsa) run on OpenMW.

engines.name: Exult (Ultima VII)
engines.how: Ultima VII's data (STATIC/U7CHUNKS...) runs on Exult.

engines.name: XnGine (Daggerfall)
engines.how: The Elder Scrolls II: Daggerfall's ARENA2 folder runs on Daggerfall Unity. Other XnGine games have no open runtime.

engines.name: Stratagus
engines.how: Stratagus games (Wargus, Stargus...) are Lua data for the open source Stratagus engine. Wargus needs data extracted from the original Warcraft II.

engines.name: NScripter
engines.how: NScripter novels (nscript.dat, .nsa archives) run on ONScripter.

engines.name: OHRRPGCE
engines.how: The game's .rpg file runs on the OHRRPGCE player (open source) for every platform.

engines.name: M.U.G.E.N
engines.how: M.U.G.E.N content (chars/, stages/, data/mugen.cfg) runs on Ikemen GO.

engines.name: Aleph One (Marathon)
engines.how: Marathon's Shapes, Sounds and Map files run on Aleph One.

engines.name: FreeSpace 2 (Source Code Project)
engines.how: FreeSpace 2's .vp archives run on FreeSpace Open.

engines.name: RPG Maker 2000/2003
engines.how: RPG_RT games run on EasyRPG Player.

engines.name: MonoGame / XNA
engines.how: XNA games run on macOS and Linux with FNA (an open reimplementation of XNA); MonoGame DesktopGL builds are already cross-platform .NET. No Porting Toolkit plugin for it yet.

engines.name: Blender Game Engine
engines.how: UPBGE, the community continuation of the Blender Game Engine, can run many .blend games; older files may need changes. No Porting Toolkit plugin for it yet. UPBGE publishes only weekly builds, which cannot be pinned, so there is no plugin yet.

engines.name: Adobe Flash (SWF)
engines.how: Flash games run in Ruffle (web or desktop). Games built on Stage3D (Starling, Flare3D, Away3D) are not supported by Ruffle yet.

engines.name: Flixel
engines.how: Flixel games are Flash (.swf): the flash-export plugin runs them with Ruffle. HaxeFlixel builds are native or HTML5.

engines.name: Starling Framework
engines.how: Starling draws with Flash's Stage3D, which Ruffle does not support yet, so there is no open runtime for it today.

engines.name: Flare3D
engines.how: Flare3D draws with Flash's Stage3D, which Ruffle does not support yet, so there is no open runtime for it today.

engines.name: Scratch
engines.how: Scratch projects (.sb3) become web or desktop apps with the TurboWarp Packager.

engines.name: TIC-80
engines.how: TIC-80 carts (.tic) run on the open source TIC-80 for every platform.

engines.name: Pyrogenesis (0 A.D.)
engines.how: 0 A.D. is open source and released for every platform; mods are data for it.

engines.name: OpenClonk
engines.how: OpenClonk is open source for every platform; scenarios are data for it.

engines.name: Qfusion (Warsow)
engines.how: Qfusion and Warsow are open source; the basewsw/ data runs on them.

engines.name: Cube Engine
engines.how: Cube is open source; the packages/ folder runs with Cube built for the target.

engines.name: Cube 2 Engine (Sauerbraten)
engines.how: Cube 2: Sauerbraten is open source and released for every platform; the packages/ folder is data for it.

engines.name: StepMania
engines.how: Songs (.sm, .ssc) play in ITGmania or StepMania on every platform. No plugin yet: ITGmania for Windows is an installer only.

engines.name: Visual Pinball
engines.how: Visual Pinball X is open source, with standalone builds for macOS and Linux; tables (.vpx) are data for it. No plugin yet: tables usually also need VPinMAME ROMs and backglass files.

engines.name: Serious Engine
engines.how: Serious Engine 1 (The First and Second Encounter) is open source; its .gro data runs on SeriousSamClassic. Later Serious Engine versions need the source. No plugin yet: its Windows builds are 7z archives without checksums.

engines.name: HPL Engine (Frictional Games)
engines.how: Penumbra and Amnesia already ship for macOS and Linux, and their HPL engines are open source (GPL). No Porting Toolkit plugin for it yet.

engines.name: Gold Box (SSI)
engines.how: Gold Box games are DOS programs (.DAX data): they run in DOSBox.

engines.name: Defold
engines.how: Defold's game archive (game.arcd, game.projectc) is platform independent; the open Defold engine of the same version runs it. No Porting Toolkit plugin for it yet.

engines.name: Ardor3D
engines.how: Java: the game's .jar files run on any platform with a Java runtime, as long as the build ships the native libraries (LWJGL, JOGL...) for the target.

engines.name: Java 3D
engines.how: Java: the game's .jar files run on any platform with a Java runtime, as long as the build ships the native libraries (LWJGL, JOGL...) for the target.

engines.name: Kivy
engines.how: Kivy apps are Python: the app's own scripts run with Kivy for the target, if the build keeps them readable.

engines.name: Pygame
engines.how: Pygame games are Python: the scripts run with Python and pygame on any platform, if the build keeps them readable.

engines.name: Panda3D
engines.how: Panda3D games are usually Python with .bam/.egg models; they run with Panda3D for the target if the scripts are readable.

engines.name: PICO-8
engines.how: PICO-8 carts (.p8, .p8.png) run in PICO-8 itself (a paid app for every platform) or as its web export.

engines.name: Solar2D (Corona)
engines.how: Solar2D compiles Lua into resource.car; the open source Solar2D can build the project again for another platform from the source project.

engines.name: AppGameKit
engines.how: Tier 1 games are bytecode (media/bytecode.byc) for AppGameKit's player, which comes with an AppGameKit licence.

engines.name: Game Editor
engines.how: Game Editor is open source; a project (.ged) can be exported again for another platform with Game Editor itself.

engines.name: Cocos2d-x (C++)
engines.how: Cocos2d-x games written in C++ are native code and need the source. Lua and JavaScript games are detected separately; HTML5 builds (Cocos2d-html5, Cocos Creator web) are exported by the HTML5 plugins.

engines.name: Cocos2d-x (Lua)
engines.how: The game's Lua scripts (src/) and resources (res/) run with the Cocos2d-x simulator of the same version, built once from Cocos2d-x's source. Encrypted scripts (XXTEA) and games with their own C++ code run only in the game's own executable.

runtime.name: Cocos2d-x simulator (same version as the game)

engines.name: Cocos2d-x (JavaScript)
engines.how: The game's JavaScript (main.js, src/) and resources run with the Cocos2d-x simulator of the same version. Compiled .jsc scripts are encrypted and run only in the game's own executable.

runtime.name: Cocos2d-x simulator (same version as the game)

engines.name: Cocos Creator
engines.how: Web builds are exported by the HTML5 plugins. Native builds embed a customised engine and usually encrypted scripts (.jsc): a port needs the Cocos Creator project.
